bill.title: Natural resources: floodplains; predisaster flood resilience grant program; establish. Amends 1994 PA 451 (MCL 324.101 - 324.90106) by adding secs. 33709, 33710 & 33711.

posted_text:
🌊 MI HB 6431 — Michigan Cities Can Get Cash to Fight Floods

Michigan cities and tribes could get grants to tackle flood risks.

This bill creates a new program, the Predisaster Flood Resilience Grant Program, run by the Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy.

Eligible applicants – including local governments and tribes – can apply for funding to assess flood vulnerabilities, restore wetlands, and implement projects like culvert inventories and hydrological studies.

Grants can cover up to 75% of project costs, up to $300,000 or $250,000 respectively, and must be used within two years of receiving the funds.

Applicants must demonstrate how they’ll fund the remaining project costs and provide a detailed project report within 90 days of completion.

The Department will also create rules for reviewing grant applications, considering factors like past disaster declarations and flood damage.
